summary: The milestone completed 6 experiments in 0.2 minutes, including 2 compute-bound entries. The longest compute-bound entry took 0.1 minutes; the available data does not identify a causal phase.
bottlenecks_identified: Disk-mtime reconstruction with no live git-log commits prevents phase-level attribution; the data does not explain why the 0.1-minute compute-bound intake exceeded the 0.02-minute compute-bound reducer.
The GPU report records one Python inference process but no batch-size receipt, so the suggested batching opportunity cannot be audited from task-level evidence.
The record omits task-level model count and runner choice, so DualGPURunner applicability cannot be assessed.
improvements_suggested: Batch 8-16 questions per forward pass and record the effective batch size; the GPU monitor projects a 4-8x throughput improvement.
Emit per-task phase timing, GPU utilization, model count, batch size, and runner-selection receipts instead of relying only on disk-mtime reconstruction.
Use model-count-aware scheduling: keep a single GGUF model on one GPU, and use DualGPURunner only when 2 or more models run concurrently.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add 8-16-question inference batching with measured batch-size and throughput receipts.
Capture task-scoped phase and GPU telemetry for every compute-bound experiment.
Record model count and runner choice, then route concurrent multi-model work across both GPUs.
meta_reflection: The locked compute-idle field is false, and the active GPU reached 96% utilization, so GPU idle is not classified as a compute-bound bottleneck. The 45% estimate applies the lower 4x batching projection to the 0.12 compute-bound minutes within 0.2 total minutes; it is conditional because the batchable share is not recorded.
